Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `PostCode.__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` that returns `core_schema.no_info_before_validator_function(cls.validate, core_schema.str_schema())`. Import `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`; this keeps the existing normalization and validation while giving Pydantic v2 a supported schema.

Replace the `PostCode` field annotation with `Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(PostCode.validate)]`, importing `Annotated` and `BeforeValidator`. Remove the legacy `__get_validators__` method so Pydantic uses the v2 before-validator metadata to normalize and validate the postcode.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field and declare key as Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right") so Pydantic tries int before str and parses "42" as 42.
Add a @field_validator("key", mode="before") that converts string values to int when int(value) succeeds, and returns the original string when conversion raises ValueError.
Import `ConfigDict` from `pydantic` and set `model_config = ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` on `Label` so numeric inputs for `sku` are converted to strings.
Add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` to `Label` that converts numeric values to `str` and returns other values unchanged, allowing Pydantic to validate the result.
In `from_sensor`, pass `units=int(reading)` when constructing `StockLevel`, so fractional sensor readings are truncated before integer validation.
Add a `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` that returns `int(value)` for numeric inputs, truncating fractional readings before Pydantic validates the `int` field.
Replace the deprecated `parse_obj_as` import and call with `TypeAdapter(list[User]).validate_python(rows)`, importing `TypeAdapter` from `pydantic`.
Remove the `parse_obj_as` import and return `[User.model_validate(row) for row in rows]` from `load_users`, validating each input row with the Pydantic v2 API.
Replace .json(...) with .model_dump_json(...), keeping by_alias and other keyword arguments.

In `changed_fields`, replace `ProfilePatch(**raw).__fields_set__` with `ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set` to use the Pydantic v2 API while preserving explicitly supplied fields, including those set to `None`.

In `changed_fields`, create the `ProfilePatch` instance and return the sorted keys of `instance.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`. This includes explicitly supplied `None` values and avoids the deprecated `__fields_set__` attribute.

Import `field_serializer` from Pydantic and add a `@field_serializer("started")` method to `Shift` that returns `value.isoformat()`. This serializes UTC datetimes with `+00:00` instead of `Z` in `model_dump(mode="json").

Import `model_serializer` from Pydantic and add a `@model_serializer(mode="wrap")` method to `Shift`. Call the supplied handler, replace the resulting `started` value with `self.started.isoformat()`, and return the data so UTC offsets serialize as `+00:00`.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_serializer("price", when_used="json")` to `Quote` that returns `float(price)`. This makes `model_dump(mode="json")` produce a JSON number for `price`.
Annotate `price` as `Annotated[Decimal, PlainSerializer(float, return_type=float, when_used="json")]`, importing `Annotated` and `PlainSerializer`. This serializes the Decimal as a JSON number.
